### Observed differences

- The three-activity block A35/A36/A41 changed its neighbours. In the earlier window it was entered from A26 — A26's outgoing transitions went to A41, A35 and A36 in about 38, 33 and 28 per 100 — and it led on to A30, with each block member naming A30 in about 28–34 per 100 of its outgoing transitions. In the later window the block is entered from A25 — A25's transitions go to A35, A36 and A41 in about 31–33 per 100 each — and it leads on to A27 (about 31–33 per 100), while A30 has nearly vanished as a successor (under 1 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- The direct connections flipped accordingly. Earlier, A27 followed A25 immediately (distance 1 in about 99 in 100 of observed A25→A27 pairs) and A30 followed A26 only at 4–5 steps (about 93 in 100 at distance 4); in the later window A27 follows A25 at 4–5 steps (essentially all observed pairs) and A30 follows A26 immediately (about 99 in 100 at distance 1). [LAG001, LAG003]

- The entry and exit relations themselves appeared and disappeared: A26→A35/A36/A41 and A35/A36/A41→A30 were observed in about 200 traces in the earlier window and in only 1–2 traces in the later one, while A25→A35 and A35→A27 were observed once earlier and about 199 times later, mostly at distances of 1–3 steps. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

- Event positions moved consistently with this reordering: the block's mean event position moved earlier, from about 0.58 to about 0.42 of the trace, while A27 (about 0.38 to 0.47) and A26 (about 0.53 to 0.62) moved later. All five activities occur in essentially every trace in both windows (200 of 200 traces each), so participation did not change — the difference is ordering, not occurrence. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block of three activities A35, A36 and A41 changed its place in the process sequence. In the earlier window it sat between A26, which led into it within about 1–3 steps, and A30, which it reached within about 1–3 steps, while A25 passed straight on to A27; in the later window it sits between A25 and A27, A26 passes straight on to A30, and A27 and A26 consequently occur later in the trace (mean event positions up by about 0.10 and 0.09) while the block occurs earlier (down by about 0.16). The block's internal routing — each member followed by one of the other two in roughly equal shares — is the same in both windows, which fits a relocation of the block rather than a reworking of the block itself. [DIR001-DIR005, LAG001-LAG010, POS001-POS005]

This goes beyond what an unchanged process typically produces: 20 control-flow items qualified against about 0.6 expected by chance, and the appearing and disappearing relations carry about 200 observations on one side against 1–2 on the other, so sampling of rare variants does not plausibly explain them. The main limitation is that the evidence shows pairwise distances of up to five steps and event positions, not full traces: it cannot distinguish whether the three-activity block moved earlier or the A27–A26 segment moved later past it, and it does not show what lies in the segment between A27 and A26; the exact distance profiles in the minority windows of some pair items also rest on only 1–2 observations. The DIR, POS and LAG items all describe one underlying reordering, so they are consistent views of the same change rather than independent confirmations. [LAG001-LAG010]
